free_tier.stated: SIT, GRE and WireGuard tunnels with BGP-routed /48s. Free, dual-stack, dyndns2-ready.

egress.terms: no monthly byte allowance is published; the fair-use section caps speed instead: '50 Mbit/s up + down, kernel-shaped'; ingress: tcp+udp

interface_detail: the site hands out SIT, GRE and WireGuard configuration; a dyndns2 endpoint updater is offered per tunnel for dynamic IPv4
tooling: wg-quick or wireguard-tools; a plain SIT/GRE interface for the other two transports
chaining: a native WireGuard profile with no dashboard step makes it the cheapest way to put a free compute instance on a public IPv6 address with every port open.

limits.value: 50 Mbit/s up and down, kernel-shaped, per tunnel
SYN-flood and ICMP rate limits applied per tunnel automatically

binding_note: At 1 TiB/month the client needs 3.24 Mbit/s sustained; the 50 Mbit/s cap is about fifteen times that, so the speed limit does not bind at this volume and no byte quota exists. What actually constrains a workload here is the blocked-port list, which the seven kinds do not name: 'SMTP - 25 - 465 - 587 - 2525' and 'POP3/IMAP - 110 - 143 - 993 - 995' are closed, so a mail service on this prefix cannot work. Reachability is IPv6-only.

identity_cost.detail: https://tb.tahio.eu/sign-up asks for Email, Password and Full Name, with Nickname optional; no card and no phone field.

reliability_note: no SLA: 'No SLA, no uptime guarantee.' Abuse, spam or scanning gives 'instant termination, no warning.'
confidence_note: documented from the vendor page read today, including a full WireGuard profile. A measured rung needs a tunnel brought up and a UDP service reached through it, which needs an account.

evidence.proved: 'SIT, GRE and WireGuard tunnels with BGP-routed /48s. Free, dual-stack, dyndns2-ready.'
a WireGuard profile with Endpoint = tb.tahio.eu:51820 and Address 2a05:1083:bef0::1/64
'50 Mbit/s up + down, kernel-shaped' and '2 tunnels per account' under 'Free isn't unlimited'
Email, Password and Full Name are the only account fields
'Each tunnel gets two /64s from the primary pools plus a /64 from a tertiary.'

notes: The page contradicts itself on prefix size: the headline says 'BGP-routed /48s' while the network section says 'Each tunnel gets two /64s from the primary pools plus a /64 from a tertiary.' The /64 arithmetic is the concrete statement and the /48 is unexplained, so the record carries three /64s and flags the /48 as unestablished. AS198889, single PoP in Oslo, peered with Gigahost.

extras.wg_detail: the page publishes a complete WireGuard profile with 'Endpoint = tb.tahio.eu:51820', AllowedIPs ::/0 and PersistentKeepalive 25, and says 'The endpoint learns your IP from the handshake, so dynamic IPv4 routers work out of the box.'
extras.volume_stated: no monthly byte allowance is published; the fair-use section caps speed instead: '50 Mbit/s up + down, kernel-shaped'
extras.transit_note: AS198889 carries the traffic; upstream is AS56655 (Gigahost), importing a default route.
